question: How do I split several VAT rates on one supplier invoice?
answer:
To split several VAT rates on a supplier invoice:

1. Go to **Supplier invoices** and open the invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").
2. Check that **Net amount**, **Tax amount**, and **Total amount** at the top cover all rates together (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").
3. In **Cost split**, add your cost lines until they add up to the **Net amount** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").
4. In **VAT split**, pick the **VAT account** for the first rate, replace the default tax amount with that rate's specific VAT, and click **+ VAT split** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").
5. Repeat the VAT split steps for each additional rate until the VAT splits total matches the tax amount at the top (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").
6. Save as draft, submit for review, or approve the invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/split-vat, section "# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice").

# Split VAT rates on a supplier invoice

Some invoices carry several VAT rates, for example 20 % on equipment and 10 % on catering. You enter one VAT line per rate, then check that the cost lines and VAT lines match the totals on the paper invoice.

## Before you start

- You need the Production manager, Member or Company admin role. A Production manager can only work on invoices in Inbox.
- The invoice must be in Inbox or In review.
- Have the paper invoice at hand.

## Steps

1. Go to **Supplier invoices** and open the invoice.
2. Check **Net amount**, **Tax amount** and **Total amount** at the top of the form. They cover all rates together.
3. In **Cost split**, fill the **Project** and the **Accounting code** (or the **Estimate cost line**). **Amount** starts with the whole net: keep it, or type part of it. Click **+ Cost split**.
4. Add more cost lines until they add up to **Net amount**. Under the lines you read "Splits total … of …".
5. In **VAT split**, pick the **VAT account** of the first rate. **Tax amount** starts with the whole tax: replace it with this rate's VAT. Click **+ VAT split**.
6. Repeat for each other rate. Under the lines you read "VAT splits total … of …". A line that goes over the total is refused: "This would exceed the bill total. Reduce the amount".
7. Click **Save as draft** to come back later, or **Submit for review**, or **Approve** if there is no review step.

> **Note.** Example: net €1,000 = €800 at 20 % (VAT €160) + €200 at 10 % (VAT €20). **Net amount** 1,000.00, **Tax amount** 180.00. VAT lines: 160 and 20.

## What you get

**Submit for review** and **Approve** stay grey until the supplier, currency and total are filled and the scan has finished. If the cost lines, the VAT lines or the total do not match, you see "The cost split total doesn't match the invoice total. Adjust the cost split lines before submitting." It shows for any of the three mismatches. After **Approve**, the amounts are locked.

> **Warning.** If you made a mistake in a saved line, use **Remove** before you approve. A VAT line of 0.00 is allowed: it posts nothing.

## Next step

Send the invoice on: [Approve a supplier invoice](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/revision/revision-operations).

# Assign an invoice to a project, a PO line or overhead

Use this to say where a supplier invoice's cost goes: a project, a purchase order line, or overhead. You can split it across several lines.

## Before you start

- The invoice is in Inbox or In review. Choosing the **Supplier** first fills in the accounting code and narrows the cost lines.
- You are a Production manager (Inbox only), Member or Company admin. Only Members and Company admins can use **Correct**.

## Steps

1. Go to **Costs** > **Supplier invoices** and click the invoice. The **Cost split** section is on the right.
2. For general costs that belong to no project, tick **Overhead**. The **Project** choice is replaced by a fixed **Overhead** label, and **Estimate cost line** is greyed out. Go to step 5.
3. In **Project**, click **Choose a project…** and pick the project.
4. To charge a line of an estimate, click **Choose a cost line…** in **Estimate cost line**. If the list says "Pick a supplier or a project first.", choose one. Choosing a line fills in an empty project.
5. To tie the cost to a purchase order, click **Choose a PO line…** in **PO line (optional)**. It fills in whatever is still empty: project, cost line, supplier, and the amount if you typed none.
6. Without a cost line, pick an **Accounting code**. It starts with the supplier's cost account.
7. Check the **Amount**. For the first line it starts with the net amount. Lower it to leave room for other lines.
8. Click **+ Cost split**. The line appears above with "Splits total … of …".
9. Repeat steps 3 to 8 for each other line until the splits total equals the **Net amount**.

> **Note.** Charge all lines to an estimate cost line, or none of them. The splits cannot go over the net amount.

To fix a saved line, click **Correct**. Use **Remove** to delete it. **Clear** empties the row you are filling.

## What you get

The lines show "Project … · Estimate … · code · amount". Once the invoice is approved, amounts are locked. You can still change where a line books to with **Correct**, until the invoice goes out to the accounting tool.

## Next step

Check the VAT and send the invoice on: [Review bill: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/purchases/review-supplier-invoice). To create the order first, see [Add an overhead purchase order](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/purchases-p-os/add-p-o).

### The cost lines have no project

Each line of the **Cost split** needs a project, or the invoice must be general company cost. You see "Pick a project".

Adjust the cost split lines before submitting." The line "Splits total … of …" shows the gap.

1. Check the three amounts against the scanned document and correct them.
2. Change the cost split lines until they add up to the **Net amount**.
3. Do the same for the **VAT split**, against the **Tax amount**.

answer:
To update an invoice's description, use these steps:

1. Click **Invoices** in the left menu [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/update-invoice-details, section "# Update invoice details")].
2. On the invoice row, click **More actions** (three dots), then **Edit description** [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/update-invoice-details, section "# Update invoice details")].
3. Type the new text in the side panel, then click **Save** [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/update-invoice-details, section "# Update invoice details")].

*Note regarding the PO number:* Once an invoice has already been issued on a proposal, the PO number on that proposal is locked and can no longer be changed [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/sales/proposal-po, section "# Add/Edit PO: every button explained > ## Read-only banner")].

# Update invoice details

Change the description printed on an invoice, or copy the client's latest details onto it, after the invoice has been created.

## Before you start

- You need the Member or Company admin role.
- The invoice must be a real invoice. Neither action is offered on a credit note.
- To refresh the client details, first change them on the client page. See [View and edit a client](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/client/modify-client).

## Steps

### Change the description

1. Click **Invoices** in the left menu.
2. On the invoice row, click **More actions** (three dots), then **Edit description**.
3. In the side panel, type the new text. The box shows the current description. Empty the box to remove the description.
4. Click **Save**. The panel closes and the list reloads.

The text is printed on the invoice PDF, above the lines (or as this invoice's row in the payment schedule, if it has one). Preview or download the PDF again to see it.

# Record the client’s purchase order on a proposal

When your client sends a purchase order (PO) for an estimate, record it on the proposal before you invoice. Its number then prints on every invoice you generate from that proposal.

## Before you start

- You need the Member or Company admin role. Viewers do not have the **Add/Edit PO** button.
- If you have it, keep the client’s PO document at hand: PDF, image, Word or Excel, up to 8MB.

## Steps

1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Proposals**.
2. Find the proposal, for example by typing in the filter box under **Estimate** or **Client**.
3. In the **Actions** column, click **Add/Edit PO**. The **Add/Edit PO** page opens.
4. If you have the PO document, drop it on the left area, or click the area to pick it. A PDF or an image shows on the left, next to the fields. A Word or Excel file is saved but cannot be shown there.
5. Type the **PO number** printed on the client’s order.
6. Set the **PO date**. It starts on today.
7. Check the **Amount**. It starts on the proposal total and must stay equal to it.
8. Check the **Currency**. Once the proposal’s billing details are confirmed, it starts on the client’s currency and must stay that one. Before that, any currency is accepted.
9. Add **Notes** if you want, for example the client contact.
10. Click **Save**. You go back to the **Proposals** list.

To change the PO later, click **Add/Edit PO** again, change the fields and click **Save**. A new file replaces the old one: only one document is kept.

> **Warning.** Once the first invoice of the proposal is issued, the PO is locked for good. The page then shows “An invoice has already been issued on this proposal, so its PO can no longer be changed.”

## What you get

The PO is saved on the proposal. Its number appears on the invoices you generate from it. If the amount or the currency does not match, a red message under the field tells you what to fix, and nothing is saved.

## Next step

[Split a proposal into invoices](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/add-proposal). Every field and message of the PO page is in [Add/Edit PO: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/sales/proposal-po).

question: How do I create a chapter (section) and add cost lines to it?
answer:
To create a chapter and add cost lines to it in an estimate:

1. Open your estimate and find the cost line you want to turn into a chapter (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/create-section, section "Steps").
2. Double-click **§** at the left of the line (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/create-section, section "Steps").
3. If the line holds values, click **Convert** in the warning window to clear them and make it a chapter (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/create-section, section "Steps"). Type a new title in the **Name** cell if needed (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/create-section, section "Steps").
4. Double-click the **+** at the far left of the new chapter row (or a line under it) to add a new cost line below it (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/add-cost-line, section "Steps").
5. Type the **Name**, **Qty**, **Unit**, **Nb** (number of days) and **Rate** for the new cost line (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/common-feature-grid/add-cost-line, section "Steps").

# Add a cost line to an estimate

Add a line when the template has no line for a cost you need, for example a second camera.

## Before you start

- You need to be a Company admin, Member or Production manager. A Freelancer can do it in the projects they were given. Viewers cannot.
- The estimate must not be finalized, and you must not be looking at a saved version.

## Steps

1. Open the estimate. You land on the **Estimate** tab.
2. Find the line the new one should go under.
3. Double-click the **+** at the far left of that line, or click it once and press Enter. A new empty line appears right below and the grid scrolls to it.
4. Type the **Name**, then fill **Qty**, **Unit**, **Nb** (number of days) and **Rate**.
5. If the line is priced in another currency, pick it in **Currency**. See [What is the difference between a line’s currency and the estimate’s currency?](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/f-a-q/f-a-q-budget/loacal-currency-vs-budgeted-currency).

There is no right-click menu in the grid: right-click only opens your browser’s menu. Calculated lines have no **+**. Chapter rows do have one.

## What you get

**Cost** is worked out for you: quantity × days (**Nb** plus the shoot days) × rate × **Exch. Rate** when the line is in another currency, minus any discount on the line, plus overtime. If a fixed cost was typed on the line, it replaces this calculation. The totals update and everything saves by itself. If **Collapse** was on, it switches off so you can see the new line. Every column is described in [Estimate: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/projects-budgets/estimate).

## Before you start

- You need to be a Member or a Company admin. Viewers do not see the button. A Production manager sees it only on bills in the **Inbox** tab, which are not approved yet.
- The original bill must already be approved (or further along). Otherwise the credit note cannot be approved.

1. Go to **Supplier invoices** and click the original bill’s row to open it.

question: How can I add a discount to an estimate?
answer:
To add a discount to an estimate in Chedar, follow these steps:

1. Open the estimate and click **Summary** in the toolbar (or the Summary icon on the estimate row in the project page) `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/intro-summary, section "Steps")`.
2. In the Estimate summary panel, click **Apply Discount** at the bottom `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "# Apply a discount to an estimate")`.
3. In the extra rows that appear, type the total you want to charge (excluding VAT) under **Total After Discount** `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "# Apply a discount to an estimate")`.
4. Click **Save** `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "# Apply a discount to an estimate")`.

question: What do the different user roles allow people to do?
answer:
Chedar has four team member roles, ranging from the narrowest to the widest:

1. **Viewer**: 
   - **Can do:** Open and read projects, estimates, templates, clients, proposals, suppliers, purchases, and supplier invoices; reply to a to-do they are assigned to; open their own user settings and notifications. Takes no paid seat.
   - **Cannot do:** Change anything; open client invoices, reports, banking, or any company settings.
   - *(Source: https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/manage-team, section "Which role to give")*

2. **Production manager**: 
   - **Can do:** Work in projects and estimates; open templates; create purchase orders; add new suppliers (without bank details); fill in and approve supplier invoices while still in the Inbox; open their own user settings and notifications.
   - **Cannot do:** Change a template; see clients, proposals, or client invoices; see supplier invoices once they leave the Inbox; view any payments; edit, archive, or delete suppliers; open reports, banking, or company settings.
   - *(Source: https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/manage-team, section "Which role to give")*

3. **Member**: 
   - **Can do:** Handle everyday operations including projects, estimates, clients, proposals, invoices, suppliers, purchases, supplier invoices, and payments; add freelancers to a project; open visual settings, terms & conditions, document numbering, cost accounts, email templates, freelancers, and their own settings.
   - **Cannot do:** Open reports, banking, general settings, bank profiles, accounting preferences, accounting categories, electronic invoicing, team settings, or billing.
   - *(Source: https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/manage-team, section "Which role to give")*

4. **Company admin**: 
   - **Can do:** Everything a Member does, plus access reports, banking, accounting exports, every settings page (including team management), and always see every project.
   - **Cannot do:** Remove themselves as admin or leave the company without leaving another admin behind.
   - *(Source: https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/manage-team, section "Which role to give")*

question: How do I change the language, the logo or the PDF design of my documents?
answer:
To change your language, logo, or document PDF design in Chedar:

### 1. Change your language
(Note: This changes the language of the app and email notifications for your own account only [https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/getting-started/profile, section "Open your user settings"]).
1. Click your initials in the yellow circle at the top right of the screen (Account menu) and select **Account settings** [https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/getting-started/profile, section "Open your user settings"].
2. Under **Language**, click the button showing your current language and pick your preferred language from the list [https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/getting-started/profile, section "Open your user settings"].

### 2. Change your logo and PDF design (colors)
(Note: Requires Company admin or Member permissions [https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/p-d-f-design]).
1. Go to **Settings** > **Visual settings** [https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/p-d-f-design].

question: Why does 'Mark as ready' do nothing, or why can't I issue the invoice?
answer:
This happens when dates are missing, the invoice was already issued, or accounting details are incomplete (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/invoice-draft-not-ready, section "# Mark as Ready does nothing, or I cannot issue the invoice").

1. In **Proposals**, click **Generate** on the proposal row (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/sync, section "# Mark a draft as ready and issue the invoice > ## Steps").
2. Click the tab for the installment you want to issue (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/sync, section "# Mark a draft as ready and issue the invoice > ## Steps").
3. Fill in both **Invoice date** and **Due date** (or use the **+30 days**, **+45 days**, or **+60 days** buttons) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/invoice-draft-not-ready, section "# Mark as Ready does nothing, or I cannot issue the invoice > ## Causes and fixes > ### A date is missing").
4. Tick **Mark as ready**, then click **Issue invoice** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/sync, section "# Mark a draft as ready and issue the invoice > ## Steps").
5. If you see an accounting error message, make sure the client has an auxiliary account name set in **Clients**, or that a Company admin has configured the sales account numbers under **Settings** > **Accounting Categories** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/invoice-draft-not-ready, section "# Mark as Ready does nothing, or I cannot issue the invoice > ## Causes and fixes > ### The client has no accounting account").

question: How do I keep several versions of the same estimate and go back to an earlier one?
answer:
To save versions of an estimate and go back to an earlier one, follow these steps:

### How to save a version
1. Go to **Estimates** in the left menu and click the estimate name (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "Steps").
2. In the estimate toolbar, next to the calendar icon (**To do**), click the clock icon (**Versions**) to open the versions panel (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "Steps").
3. Optionally, type a description in **Label (optional)** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "Steps").
4. Click **Save version** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "Steps").

### How to go back to an earlier version
1. Open the **Versions** panel by clicking the clock icon in the estimate toolbar (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "What you get").
2. Click **Versions** on the specific version you want to view; it opens as a read-only snapshot (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "What you get").
3. Click **Duplicate as new estimate** in that version's row to create a new, editable estimate from it in the same project (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/versions, section "What you get").

4. Read the cost table, one line per section. It opens with **Budget**, **Provisional**, **Actual** and **Purchase**. Use **Show/hide columns** to add **Ordered**, **Draft orders**, **Billed**, **Expected** (the larger of the estimate budget, or billed plus what is still on order; billed plus on order alone is **Purchase**) and **Difference**. question: How do I generate a SEPA payment file for supplier payments?
answer:
To generate a SEPA payment file for your supplier invoices, follow these steps:

1. Open **Supplier invoices** in the left menu, then open the **To pay** tab (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
2. Review the list of bills. (Note: The export includes every euro bill on the **To pay** tab; if there are bills you do not want to pay yet, tick them and click **Back to pending**) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
3. Click **Export** > **SEPA** to open the **SEPA export** window (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
4. Select the bank account the money leaves from under **Bank profile** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
5. Choose the **SEPA version** (v8 is recommended unless your bank requires the older v2 version) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
6. Choose the **Mode**: **Individual** (your bank shows one line per payment) or **Batch** (one line for all payments) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
7. Fill in the **Entry date** for the payment (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
8. Tick **Update (mark exported invoices as paid)** if you want the exported bills to move automatically to the **Paid** tab (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
9. Click **Generate** to download the SEPA file (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
10. Click **Done** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").
11. Upload the generated file into your online banking platform under their SEPA transfer section (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file, section "Steps").

question: How can I limit which projects a team member can see?
answer:
You can limit project visibility for team members who have the **Viewer** or **Production manager** role (Members and Company admins always see every project) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").

1. Go to **Settings** > **Team** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
2. Ensure the person's role is set to **Production manager** or **Viewer** in the **Role** list on their row (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
3. Tick **Limit people to their assigned projects** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
4. If a window appears because some people have no projects assigned yet, click **Turn on anyway** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
5. On the person's row, click the link in the **Projects** column (such as **None** or a project count) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
6. Tick each project you want to assign to them (and optionally tick **Include everything inside** for sub-projects) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").
7. Click **Save** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/limit-member-projects, section "# Limit which projects a person can see").

question: How do social charges work on payroll cost lines in an estimate?
answer:
In Chedar, employer payroll charges are calculated automatically on estimate cost lines using assigned payroll bands and rates (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "How Chedar uses them").

### How they work:
1. **Line assignment:** Each cost line has a **Payroll** column where you select the appropriate payroll band (or **None** to charge no payroll) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "In practice").
2. **Calculation:** Chedar multiplies the line cost by the percentage rate of the assigned band and adds the result to the estimate's payroll section (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "How Chedar uses them").
3. **Insurance and Overheads:** Insurance covers are then calculated on the line cost (and often on the payroll amount as well), followed by markup and overheads (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "How Chedar uses them").

### How to adjust them:
1. Go to the **Estimate** tab.
2. Locate the **Payroll Taxes** (or equivalent) section where each band and its rate are listed (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "In practice").
3. Type the new percentage directly into the band row (type `0` to charge nothing) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "In practice").
4. Change a specific line's payroll band by selecting a different option in that line's **Payroll** column (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget-templates/360/dependencies, section "Change a rate").
5. Click **Summary** to view the aggregated **Payroll Taxes** and **Insurance** rows (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/knowledge/payroll-charges, section "In practice").

## How Chedar uses them

Chedar does not rebuild each contribution. Each cost line carries one band, and each band has one rate. Chedar multiplies the line cost by that rate and adds the result to the payroll section. Insurance is then charged on the line cost and, in most templates, on the payroll amount too.

The starting rates come from the template. For example, in the 360 Template a Shooting crew line starts at 67% and a Talent line at 58%. In the CNC template, authors start at 1.1%. These are starting values, not official rates. Check them against your payroll before you quote.

## Example

A gaffer is booked for 10 days at €1,000.00, so the line costs €10,000.00. In the 360 Template, this Shooting crew line carries a 67% band, and Civil risk insurance is at 2%. The template also starts with a No show row at 1%. It is left out here to keep the example short.

| Step | Calculation | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Line cost | 10 days x €1,000.00 | €10,000.00 |
| Payroll charges | 67% of €10,000.00 | €6,700.00 |
| Civil risk insurance | 2% of (€10,000.00 + €6,700.00) | €334.00 |
| Cost with charges |  | €17,034.00 |

A talent line of €5,000.00 on a 58% band adds €2,900.00 in charges. The margin and overheads are added afterwards, in the **Markup & Overheads** row of the summary.

# Payroll charges in a production estimate

In France, every salary you pay in a production also costs the employer contributions on top. Chedar adds them to the estimate from a rate you can see and change, so the total shows the real cost of your crew and cast.

## What the charges are

Employer contributions are paid on top of gross pay. The URSSAF lists them one by one. Among them:

- health, maternity, disability and death cover: 13% in most cases, 7% when annual pay is at most 2.5 times the Smic as it stood on 31 December 2023 (about 2.34 times the Smic since 1 June 2026);
- family allowances: 5.25% in most cases, 3.45% when annual pay is at most 3.5 times the Smic as it stood on 31 December 2023 (about 3.28 times the Smic since 1 June 2026);
- work accident and occupational illness: a rate set for each establishment by the Carsat (the Cramif in Île-de-France, the CGSS overseas), based on its size and activity;
- the employer contribution to social dialogue: 0.016%.

Retirement and unemployment contributions come on top of these. In film and TV, paid leave is also collected by the Caisse des congés spectacles, run by Audiens.

> **Note.** The rates above are the URSSAF's general ones at the time of writing. They change, and some depend on pay level. Your payroll provider, Audiens or the URSSAF gives the exact figure for each person.

question: How do I edit the categories and cost lines of a template?
answer:
To edit the categories and cost lines of a template:

1. Go to **Templates**, click the template you want to change, and click **Edit** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").
2. To edit a cell (**Name**, **Qty**, **Nb**, **Rate**, etc.), click it, type your change, and press Enter (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").
3. To add a new cost line, click the **+** button on the row directly above where you want the line to appear (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").
4. To create a section/chapter heading, click the **§** button on a line (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").
5. To rename a chapter, click its **Name** cell, type the new name, and press Enter (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").
6. Click **Publish** to make your changes live for new estimates (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/templates/edit-template, section "Edit an estimate template").

# What is the difference between a line’s currency and the estimate’s currency?

The estimate has one currency for all its totals. Each cost line can be priced in another currency, with its own exchange rate. Chedar converts the line into the estimate currency.

## The estimate currency

You set it in **Edit Budget** > **Financial parameters** > **Currency**. Every total, the margins and the PDF use it.

## The line currency

On the **Estimate** tab, each line has a **Rate**, a **Currency** and an **Exch. Rate** column.

- **Rate** is the price in the line currency.
- **Exch. Rate** turns one unit of the line currency into the estimate currency. When you pick a **Currency**, Chedar fills it by itself.
- **Cost** is already converted: quantity × days × rate × exchange rate, plus overtime.

For example, the estimate is in euros and a camera is hired in London: **Qty** 1, **Nb** 2, **Rate** 1,000. You pick **GBP** and the exchange rate is 1.15. **Cost** shows €2,300.

question: How do I mark an invoice as paid, and what do the invoice statuses mean?
answer:
Assuming you are asking about **client invoices**, here is how to mark one as paid and what the different statuses mean.

### How to mark a client invoice as paid
*(Requires Member or Company admin role)*

1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Invoices** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "# Mark an invoice as paid").
2. Find the invoice (its status will be **Pending**, **Overdue**, or **Credit note issued**) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "# Mark an invoice as paid").
3. In the **Actions** column, click the **Mark paid** icon (a tick in a circle) to open the **Mark as paid** window (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "# Mark an invoice as paid").
4. Check or change the **Paid date** to match the day the money arrived (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "# Mark an invoice as paid").
5. Click **Confirm** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "# Mark an invoice as paid").

*(Note: If you use the bank feed under **Banking**, reconciling matching bank payments to the invoice will also automatically mark it as paid) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/mark-paid, section "Before you start").*

---

### What the invoice statuses mean

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Pending** | The invoice is not paid, and its due date has not yet passed (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |
| **Overdue** | The invoice is not paid, and the due date has passed (starting the day after) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |
| **Paid** | The invoice has been marked as paid manually, or matched via bank reconciliation (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |
| **Credit note issued** | Part of the invoice is covered by a credit note (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |
| **Fully credited** | Credit notes cover the entire invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |
| **Credit note** | The row itself represents a credit note (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/invoices-list, section "What the status tells you"). |

# Mark an invoice as paid

When a client has paid, record it on the invoice so the list shows it as paid, with the payment date.

## Before you start

- You need the Member or Company admin role.
- If the payment is in your bank feed, reconcile it from **Banking** instead. Once the bank payments matched to the invoice cover its full amount, it is marked paid by itself, on the date of the last payment, and your accounts stay in line.

## Steps

1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Invoices**.
2. Find the invoice. Its status is **Pending**, **Overdue** or **Credit note issued**.
3. In the **Actions** column, click the **Mark paid** icon (a tick in a circle). The **Mark as paid** window opens.
4. Check the **Paid date**. It starts on today; change it to the day the money arrived.
5. Click **Confirm**. The status changes to **Paid** and the date shows in the **Paid date** column.

> **Note.** A credit note has no **Mark paid** icon.

## Undo a payment

1. On the paid invoice, click the **Mark unpaid** icon (a curved arrow).
2. The window asks “Revert this invoice to Pending/Overdue?”. Click **Confirm**.

The status goes back to **Pending**, or **Overdue** if the due date has passed, and the paid date is cleared.

## What you get

The invoice no longer counts as waiting for payment. If a credit note was issued on it, the status still shows **Credit note issued** or **Fully credited**, and the **Paid date** column shows the payment.

## Next step

[Export client invoices](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/export-invoices) for your accountant. To reconcile payments from the bank feed, see [Banking: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/bank-accounting/banking).

# The Invoices list: where your client invoices live

The **Invoices** page gathers every invoice and credit note your company has issued to clients. It does not create invoices: it is where you follow them once issued, until they are paid and exported to your accounts. You open it from **Invoices** in the left menu, under **Revenues**.

## Where an invoice comes from

An invoice starts as an estimate. You move the estimate to **Proposals**, then use **Generate** to split its total into installments and issue each one. Once issued, the invoice appears on **Invoices**. A credit note you create from an invoice appears there too, on its own row, with its amount in parentheses.

## What the status tells you

Each row has one status, worked out by the app from the payment and the due date:

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| **Pending** | Not paid, and the due date has not passed. |
| **Overdue** | Not paid, from the day after the due date. |
| **Paid** | Someone marked it paid, or bank payments reconciled in Banking cover its full amount. |
| **Credit note issued** | Part of the invoice is covered by a credit note. |
| **Fully credited** | Credit notes cover the whole invoice. |
| **Credit note** | The row is a credit note. |

Once a credit note exists, the credit status wins: the row shows **Credit note issued** or **Fully credited** even when the invoice is paid. The **Paid date** column still shows the payment.

Example: invoice 2026-041 of €18,000.00 for a commercial shoot, due on 30 September. On 1 October it turns **Overdue**. The client pays €18,000.00 on 8 October and the bank payment is reconciled in Banking: it shows **Paid**, with 8 October as the paid date.

question: Which email notifications can I turn on or off?
answer:
You can turn three types of email notifications on or off in Chedar (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/notifications, section "Choose which emails you receive"):

1. **Email me about overdue to-dos** (under *To-do email reminders*): A daily round-up at 9am Paris time for to-dos you are subscribed to. *Off by default.*
2. **Email me when somebody replies** (under *Replies to your to-dos*): An email whenever someone answers a to-do you wrote or replied to. *On by default.*
3. **Email me tips while my company is new** (under *Getting started emails*): Tips during your first weeks and before your trial ends (sent only to the person who signed the company up while they are a Company admin). *On by default.*

### How to change them:
1. Click **Settings** > **Notifications** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/notifications, section "Steps").
2. Tick or untick the boxes to turn each notification on or off. Each box saves instantly as you click it.

question: After issuing a deposit invoice, the estimate changed. How do I update the balance invoice without losing the deposit?
answer:
To update the balance invoice after an estimate changes without losing the deposit, Chedar automatically brings amounts in line with the new estimate total for any installments that have not yet been issued (already issued invoices are never touched) [5, 1].

1. Open **Proposals** under **Revenues** in the left menu [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/create-proposal, section "Steps")].
2. Find the proposal row and click **Refresh** to re-read the estimate, update the proposal total, and recalculate any unbilled installments [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/sales/proposals, section "Row buttons")].
3. Click **Generate** on the proposal row [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/sales/proposals, section "Row buttons")].
4. Go to the tab for the balance installment, check the updated amount, and fill in your invoice and due dates [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/sync, section "Steps")].
5. Tick **Mark as ready**, then click **Issue invoice** [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/proposals/sync, section "Steps")].

# From estimate to invoice

Billing a client follows one path: estimate, proposal, invoice drafts, invoices, then credit notes if something must be corrected. Each step has its own screen, its own statuses and its own rights.

## Who can do what

- **Company admin** and **Member**: every step below, from moving an estimate to Proposals through to credit notes.

| Step | Where | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimate | Project | Your quote to the client. Any active estimate that is not expired can be billed. |
| Proposal | **Proposals** | One proposal per estimate. It holds the amount to bill. |
| Invoice drafts | **Generate invoices** | You split the proposal into installments. Each installment is a draft. |
| Invoice | **Invoices** | A draft that is issued becomes a numbered invoice. |
| Credit note | **Invoices** | A correction against an issued invoice. |

question: How do I set up e-invoicing and check that my clients will receive invoices through it?
answer:
To set up e-invoicing and check that your clients will receive invoices through it:

### Set up e-invoicing

1. Go to **Settings** > **Electronic invoicing** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "# Set up e-invoicing").
2. Type your 9-digit **SIREN** in **Company legal details for electronic invoicing**, click **Fill from the registry**, check the details, and type your **Share capital** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "# Set up e-invoicing").
3. Fill in the **Onboarding contact** details (**First name**, **Last name**, **Job title**, and **Email**) and click **Save legal details** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "# Set up e-invoicing").
4. Under **Sending provider: Sage Network**, choose your Kbis file, click **Submit Kbis**, pick your **Business type**, tick the authorization box, and click **Onboard** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "# Set up e-invoicing"). *(Optional)* Connect **Billit** below if you also have clients with neither a French VAT number nor a SIREN in France (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "# Set up e-invoicing").
5. Once Sage shows **Connected**, click **Check integration health** to review the health dashboard (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/e-invoicing, section "Check the connection").

---

### Check that your clients will receive invoices through it

Chedar automatically sends invoices when issued based on your client's details (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "# Send an e-invoice"):
* **Sage Network** is used if Sage is connected and the client has a **French VAT number** (format: `FR` followed by two characters and the nine SIREN digits) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/client/add-client, section "## What invoicing and e-invoicing need").
* **Billit** is used if Billit is connected and the client does *not* have a French VAT number (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "## Clients without a French VAT number (Billit)").
* Nothing is sent if neither provider is connected (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "# Send an e-invoice").

**To check an invoice's delivery status:**
1. Go to **Invoices** in the left menu (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "## Steps").
2. Look at the e-invoice icon on the invoice row. A green **E-invoice sent** status means Chedar is sending it or Sage has received it (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "## Steps").
3. Click the icon to open the **E-invoicing status** window, where you can view the specific status ("pending", "submitted", "delivered", or "accepted") and click **Refresh status** to fetch the latest update from Sage (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/send-e-invoice, section "## Steps").

question: How do I compare budget and actual costs on a billed production, and what do the margin figures mean?
answer:
To compare budget and actual costs on a billed production in Chedar:

1. Open your estimate and click the **Actual** tab at the bottom (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/grid-wrap, section "Steps").
2. Type the real cost of each line in the **Actual** column (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/grid-wrap, section "Steps").
3. Click **Show totals & margins** at the top to view the comparison strip (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/grid-wrap, section "Steps").
4. Click **Summary** to see the **Actual variation** and **Provisional variation** (the gap to the budget in € and %, where positive means you spent more than budgeted) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/grid-wrap, section "Steps").

### What the margin figures mean

* **Margin amount:** The price of the production (after discount, excluding VAT) minus the total cost (including social charges and insurance) (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/introduction, section "How the three figures differ"; https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/total-costs, section "The totals bar on the Provisional and Actual tabs").
* **Margin %:** The margin divided by the price (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/introduction, section "How the three figures differ").
* **Budget margin:** The locked margin from your original estimate (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/introduction, section "How the three figures differ").
* **Provisional margin:** The planned margin based on your forecasts (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/introduction, section "How the three figures differ"; https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/portfolio-margin, section "What you get").
* **Actual margin:** The estimate total minus your entered real costs (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/portfolio-margin, section "What you get"). 
* **Red figures:** Any negative margin displays in red (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/actuals/introduction, section "How the three figures differ").

Section: # Budget, provisional and actual: how Chedar tracks a project's cost > ## How the three figures differ

## How the three figures differ

- **Budget** is the locked amount from the **Estimate** tab. It does not move when you forecast or spend.
- **Provisional** is your forecast. You type the total, or you click **Add col.** to enter quantity, days and rate and let the app calculate it. A line left empty means nothing was forecast. It shows blank, not 0.
- **Actual** is the real cost of the line, typed by you. It is not filled in from supplier bills.
- **Purchase** is separate. It adds up the supplier bills given to the line, before VAT. A bill counts even if it is still in Inbox or In review.

## An example

You quote a short film at €50,000 (price after discount, excluding VAT). The line "Chef opérateur" is budgeted at €12,000. The camera team asks for more, so you set **Provisional** to €13,500. At the end, the invoice comes to €14,200, so you type that in **Actual**. Other lines move too, so the totals below change by more than this one line.

Across the whole estimate, the totals bar shows the effect on the margin. It is closed at first: click **Show totals & margins**.

|  | Cost | Margin | Margin % |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Budget margin** | €38,000 | €12,000 | 24% |
| **Provisional margin** | €41,000 | €9,000 | 18% |
| **Actual margin** | €43,500 | €6,500 | 13% |

The margin is the price minus the cost, and the percentage is the margin divided by the price. A negative margin shows in red. A tier with nothing entered yet shows a cost of 0 and a margin equal to the whole price.

Use this page to compare the margin of all your active estimates with a target you set.

## Before you start

- Only a Company admin can see and open this page.

## Steps

1. Go to **Reports** > **Portfolio Margin**.
2. Pick **Provisional (planned)** or **Actual (real costs)**. The page recalculates at once.
3. Pick a period: **This month**, **Year to date** or **All time**, or fill **From** and **To**. Dates apply to the day the estimate was created.
4. To narrow the list, switch on **Draft**, **Finalized**, **Billed** or **Expired** (none on shows all four). **Starred** keeps only estimates counted in their project’s totals.
5. Set **Target margin** with the slider or the box. It starts at 25% and goes back to 25% when you reload the page.
6. Read the four figures: **Blended margin** (the whole selection, weighted by amount), **Total tracked value** (sum of the estimate totals), **Below target** (how many are under your target) and **At-risk value** (total of those more than 3 points under).

How budget and real costs feed the margin:

- **Provisional (planned)**: the margin planned in the estimate, from the budget alone.
- **Actual (real costs)**: the estimate total minus the real costs entered so far, payroll charges, levies and insurance included. With no real costs yet it shows 100%; a total of 0 shows 0%.

question: I issued an invoice with the wrong VAT rate. How do I cancel it and issue a corrected one?
answer:
To correct a client invoice issued with the wrong VAT rate, you need to issue a credit note to cancel the incorrect invoice, and then issue a new, corrected invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/intro, section "5. Credit notes").

### Steps

1. **Issue a credit note for the incorrect invoice:**
   * Go to **Invoices** in the left menu (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/credit-note).
   * Click **Credit note** on the invoice's actions or under **More actions** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/credit-note).
   * Enter the full credit amount to fully credit the invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/intro, section "5. Credit notes").
   * Confirm to create the credit note (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/credit-note).

2. **Issue the corrected invoice:**
   * Create a new invoice with the correct VAT rate and details, then send it to your client (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/update-invoice-details, section "Next step").

# Record a supplier credit note

Use this when a supplier cancels a whole bill and sends you a credit note. Chedar links the credit note to the original bill and, once approved, cancels that bill’s accounting entry.

## Before you start

- You need to be a Member or a Company admin. Viewers do not see the button. A Production manager sees it only on bills in the **Inbox** tab, which are not approved yet.
- The original bill must already be approved (or further along). Otherwise the credit note cannot be approved.
- The credit note must cover the whole bill. Only one credit note per bill is allowed.

## Steps

1. Go to **Supplier invoices** and click the original bill’s row to open it.
2. At the bottom of the page, click **+ Credit note**. The **Create credit note** window opens. The currency is the bill’s and cannot be changed.
3. Check **Net amount**, **Tax amount** and **Total amount**. They are already filled with the bill’s amounts as negatives. Leave them as they are.
4. Optional: type **Their invoice number (optional)** and pick **Invoice date (optional)**.
5. Click **Create credit note**. A white pop-up at the bottom of the screen says “Credit note created” and the credit note lands in the **Inbox** tab, with a **Credit note** badge.
6. Approve it from the list: on its row in the **Inbox** tab, click the **Approve** icon. If your company reviews bills first, click **Submit for review**, then **Approve** in the **Review** tab.

> **Note.** The credit note’s own page is read-only: approve it from its row in the list.

> **Warning.** If you change an amount, the window warns that it does not exactly reverse the original. You can still create it, but if the total differs, approving it will fail. The total must also equal net plus tax, or **Create credit note** stays grey.

## What you get

The credit note shows in the list with the bill’s supplier and its total in brackets. Once approved, the original bill’s accounting entry is reversed.

## Next step

Approve the credit note, then export it with your other bills: [Export supplier invoices to accounting](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices).

# Mark an invoice as paid

When a client has paid, record it on the invoice so the list shows it as paid, with the payment date.

## Before you start

- You need the Member or Company admin role.
- If the payment is in your bank feed, reconcile it from **Banking** instead. Once the bank payments matched to the invoice cover its full amount, it is marked paid by itself, on the date of the last payment, and your accounts stay in line.

## Steps

1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Invoices**.
2. Find the invoice. Its status is **Pending**, **Overdue** or **Credit note issued**.
3. In the **Actions** column, click the **Mark paid** icon (a tick in a circle). The **Mark as paid** window opens.
4. Check the **Paid date**. It starts on today; change it to the day the money arrived.
5. Click **Confirm**. The status changes to **Paid** and the date shows in the **Paid date** column.

> **Note.** A credit note has no **Mark paid** icon.

## Undo a payment

1. On the paid invoice, click the **Mark unpaid** icon (a curved arrow).
2. The window asks “Revert this invoice to Pending/Overdue?”. Click **Confirm**.

The status goes back to **Pending**, or **Overdue** if the due date has passed, and the paid date is cleared.

## What you get

The invoice no longer counts as waiting for payment. If a credit note was issued on it, the status still shows **Credit note issued** or **Fully credited**, and the **Paid date** column shows the payment.

1. Go to **Costs** > **Supplier invoices** and click the invoice. The **Cost split** section is on the right.
2. For general costs that belong to no project, tick **Overhead**. The **Project** choice is replaced by a fixed **Overhead** label, and **Estimate cost line** is greyed out. Go to step 5.
3. In **Project**, click **Choose a project…** and pick the project.

7. Check the **Amount**. For the first line it starts with the net amount. Lower it to leave room for other lines.
8. Click **+ Cost split**. The line appears above with "Splits total … of …".
9. Repeat steps 3 to 8 for each other line until the splits total equals the **Net amount**.

# Approve a supplier invoice

Approving books the invoice in your accounts and moves it forward, ready to be marked to pay.

## Before you start

- You need to be a Member or a Company admin. A Production manager can approve only invoices still in Inbox, and only when your company does not use the review step.
- If your company uses the review step, the invoice must be In review. If it does not, you can also approve it straight from Inbox.

## Steps

1. Go to **Supplier invoices** and open the invoice from the **Review** tab (or the **Inbox** tab if your company does not use the review step). The scan is on the left, the form on the right.
2. Wait until the banner "OCR is still reading this bill. Wait for it to finish, or run it again if it seems stuck." is gone. If the scan cannot be read, click **Skip OCR** and type the fields yourself.
3. Check that **Supplier**, **Currency** and **Total amount** are filled. **Total amount** must equal **Net amount** plus **Tax amount**, minus any reverse-charge VAT (that VAT is not in the total).
4. Check the **Cost split**: the lines must add up to the **Net amount**, and the **VAT split** to the **Tax amount**. For each line, fill in a **Project** (not needed under **Overhead**) and an **Accounting code** or an **Estimate cost line**. Either every line has an estimate cost line, or none does.
5. Click **Approve**. The invoice is saved, booked and the page closes.
6. If a window asks **Approve anyway?**, the invoice looks like one already on file. Click **Approve anyway** only if it is really a second invoice. Click **Go back** to check first.

> **Warning.** After **Approve**, the amounts are locked and the invoice is booked in the accounts. To undo it, use **Reopen** in the invoice list.

## What you get

The invoice is now Approved. You find it in the **Pending & overdue** tab. To get it into **To pay**, use **Mark to pay** there.

If **Approve** stays greyed out or an error appears in red, read the error messages and the rules for the buttons at the bottom in [Review bill: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/purchases/review-supplier-invoice).

## Next step

Mark the invoice to pay from the list: [Supplier invoices: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/purchases/supplier-invoices).

If **Approve** stays greyed out or an error appears in red, see [I cannot approve a supplier invoice](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/cannot-approve).

### How to export a month of supplier invoices

1. Go to **Costs** > **Supplier invoices** and open the **Not exported** tab [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices, section "Steps")].
2. Click **Export**, then **Accounting** [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices, section "Steps")].
3. Choose your accounting format (**FEC**, **Sage 100**, **Sage 100 Online**, **Sage Révision Expert**, or **Full CSV**) [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices, section "Steps")].
4. Set **From** and **To** to cover the month you want to export [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices, section "Steps")].
5. Click **Not yet exported** to download the file and mark those invoices as exported [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/export-invoices/export-invoices, section "Steps")].

---

### How to check that the account numbers are right

* **Check general supplier and client accounts:** Go to **Settings** > **Accounting Categories** and check the **Supplier Cost Account Number** (typically 401000) and client sales accounts [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/accounting-parameters/9-misc-account-numbers, section "Steps")].
* **Check cost accounts catalog:** Go to **Settings** > **Cost accounts** to review your custom cost accounts and labels [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/accounting-parameters/cost-account-numbers, section "Steps")].
* **Check default supplier cost accounts:** Go to **Settings** > **Accounting preferences** to verify the **Default supplier cost account** applied to new suppliers and unassigned lines [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/accounting-parameters/cost-account-numbers, section "Steps")].
* **Check VAT accounts:** On **Settings** > **Accounting Categories**, check the **VAT accounts on purchases** used by supplier invoices [(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/settings/account-settings/accounting-parameters/cost-account-numbers, section "Steps")].

# Export supplier invoices to accounting

Send your booked supplier invoices to your accounting software as a file, and keep track of what has already gone out.

## Before you begin

- In the **Export** menu, only a Company admin sees **Accounting**. A Member also sees [Export a SEPA payment file](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/purchases/sepa-payment-file). A Viewer or Production manager sees only **Export CSV**.
- The invoice must be approved. Invoices still in the **Inbox** or **Review** tab have nothing to export yet. The **Review** tab appears only when **Review supplier invoices before exporting** is on in **Settings** > **Accounting preferences**.

## Steps

1. Go to **Costs** > **Supplier invoices** and open the **Not exported** tab. It lists the approved, to pay and paid invoices that no export has picked up yet.
2. Click **Export**, then **Accounting**. The **Export to accounting** window opens.
3. In **Format**, choose **FEC**, **Sage 100**, **Sage 100 Online**, **Sage Révision Expert** or **Full CSV**.
4. Set **From** and **To** to limit the dates. Leave both empty to export every date.
5. For **Sage 100 Online** only, tick the **Analytic axes** you want: **Quote number**, **Project number**, **Owner**, **Extra analytic axis**, **Third axis**.
6. Click **Not yet exported** to get only what has not gone out before. Click **Export all matching** to get everything in the dates, including invoices already exported.
7. Your browser downloads the file. Whichever button you used, the invoices in it are marked as exported and leave the **Not exported** tab.

> **Note.** The window only uses the dates you set. The search, tabs and filters of the page are not applied.

## What you get

| Format | File |
| --- | --- |
| **FEC**, **Sage 100**, **Sage 100 Online** | Text file (.txt) |
| **Sage Révision Expert**, **Full CSV** | CSV file (.csv) |

The file name starts with AC, then the format and the date. **Export CSV** in the same menu gives a spreadsheet of the whole list as filtered, every page, instead. That one is not an accounting export.

> **Warning.** The cost split of an invoice already sent to accounting can no longer be corrected. Raise a credit note instead.

## Next step

Pay the invoices that are ready in [Supplier invoices: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/purchases/supplier-invoices).

question: Why can't I find my invoices from 2023 in the app?
answer:
By default, the client invoices and supplier invoices lists only load recent dates (such as the current year or the last month), so older invoices from 2023 are hidden until you widen the date range or period.

**For client invoices:**
1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Invoices** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/filter, section "# Filter invoices").
2. Set the **From** and **To** date filters to cover the year 2023 (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/invoicing-proposals/invoices/filter, section "# Filter invoices").

**For supplier invoices:**
1. Click **Supplier invoices** in the left menu (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/filter-invoices, section "# Filter supplier invoices").
2. Next to **Filter dates on**, choose **Created** or **Invoice date** (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/filter-invoices, section "# Filter supplier invoices").
3. Select a longer period such as **1 year**, **All time**, or use **Custom** to include 2023 (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/suppliers-purchases-purchase-orders/supplier-invoices/filter-invoices, section "# Filter supplier invoices").

question: The total looks wrong after merging estimates: a discount line is missing. Is this a bug?
answer:
The new estimate takes its header, bid letter, rates, overtime hours, and insurance settings **only from the base estimate** you selected in Step 3 `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/projects-budgets/merge-estimates-into-a-new-estimate, section "Merge estimates into a new estimate")`. If the discount was on one of the other estimates you merged rather than the base estimate, it is not carried over automatically in the same way.

To re-apply the discount:
1. Open the merged estimate and go to the estimate summary `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "Apply a discount to an estimate")`.
2. Click **Apply Discount** `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "Apply a discount to an estimate")`.
3. In **Total After Discount**, type the total you want to charge excluding VAT `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "Apply a discount to an estimate")`.
4. Click **Save** `(https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/film-budget/summary/discount, section "Apply a discount to an estimate")`.

Merge several estimates of one project into a new estimate. The estimates you pick do not change.

## Before you start

- You can add estimates in the project (Production manager, Member, Company admin, or a Freelancer inside their project). Your plan must include estimates.

5. Read the check screen. It shows the name of the new estimate, what each estimate adds, the number of lines copied, the new total and, if any, the discounts carried over.

question: Is an invoice legally valid if issued without a PO number?
answer:
The help centre confirms that a missing purchase order number does not block an invoice in Chedar, as the PO number is optional and its absence will not prevent you from issuing an invoice (https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/sales/invoice-draft-not-ready, section "The PO number is missing"). 

However, because legal validity depends on external accounting and tax regulations, the help centre does not cover whether an invoice is legally valid without a PO number. Please contact Chedar support or consult your legal/accounting advisor for guidance on local invoicing regulations.

# Record the client’s purchase order on a proposal

When your client sends a purchase order (PO) for an estimate, record it on the proposal before you invoice. Its number then prints on every invoice you generate from that proposal.

## Before you start

- You need the Member or Company admin role. Viewers do not have the **Add/Edit PO** button.
- If you have it, keep the client’s PO document at hand: PDF, image, Word or Excel, up to 8MB.

## Steps

1. In the left menu, under **Revenues**, click **Proposals**.
2. Find the proposal, for example by typing in the filter box under **Estimate** or **Client**.
3. In the **Actions** column, click **Add/Edit PO**. The **Add/Edit PO** page opens.
4. If you have the PO document, drop it on the left area, or click the area to pick it. A PDF or an image shows on the left, next to the fields. A Word or Excel file is saved but cannot be shown there.
5. Type the **PO number** printed on the client’s order.
6. Set the **PO date**. It starts on today.
7. Check the **Amount**. It starts on the proposal total and must stay equal to it.
8. Check the **Currency**. Once the proposal’s billing details are confirmed, it starts on the client’s currency and must stay that one. Before that, any currency is accepted.
9. Add **Notes** if you want, for example the client contact.
10. Click **Save**. You go back to the **Proposals** list.

To change the PO later, click **Add/Edit PO** again, change the fields and click **Save**. A new file replaces the old one: only one document is kept.

> **Warning.** Once the first invoice of the proposal is issued, the PO is locked for good. The page then shows “An invoice has already been issued on this proposal, so its PO can no longer be changed.”

## What you get

The PO is saved on the proposal. Its number appears on the invoices you generate from it. If the amount or the currency does not match, a red message under the field tells you what to fix, and nothing is saved.

# Issue a purchase order and send it to the supplier

Issuing gives a draft purchase order (PO) its number. Then you download the PDF and send it to the supplier.

## Before you start

- You are a Company admin, a Member or a Production manager.
- The draft has a supplier and at least one line.

## Steps

1. In the left menu, click **Purchase orders**. The page is titled **Purchases & POs**. Click your draft. The title reads **Draft: no number yet**.
2. Check the **Supplier**, **Delivery date**, **Delivery address** and the lines. Add any terms in **Comments**.
3. Tick **Mark as ready to issue**. The **Issue** button appears.
4. Click **Issue**. There is no second question.
5. A message above the form reads "Issued as" followed by the PO number. The status becomes Issued and the PDF is redone with the number.
6. Click **Download PDF**. The file is named after the PO number.
7. Send the file to the supplier from your own mailbox. Chedar has no button to email a PO.

> **Warning.** Issuing uses up the PO number and freezes the lines. It cannot be undone. If the order will not happen, use **Void**: the number is kept but the order no longer counts.

## What you get

- The supplier, the dates and every quantity and rate are frozen.
- You can still change **Comments** and each line **Description**, for example to fix a typo. Download the PDF again afterwards.
- An issued PO cannot be deleted, only voided.
- The billing and payment chips are worked out from the supplier invoices linked to the PO lines. You never set them by hand.

## Next step

When the supplier invoice arrives, open it and, in **Cost split**, pick this PO's line in **PO line (optional)**. The chip reads Billed once linked invoices cover every line, and Paid once they are all paid. See [Review bill: every button explained](https://learn.chedar.io/en/docs/screens/purchases/review-supplier-invoice).

Set who is in charge of an estimate, so everyone knows who follows it and you can filter the list by person.
